agency.name: North Carolina Department of Transportation, Division of Motor Vehicles (NCDMV)

exam.roadSigns: Separate traffic-sign recognition test: Class C applicants must correctly identify 9 of 12 road signs (Class A/B: all signs) by color and shape and explain each (19A NCAC 03B .0201; NCDMV Driver License Tests page).
exam.format: Automated computer knowledge test on traffic laws and safe-driving practice, taken at a driver license office (walk-ins or appointments at skiptheline.ncdot.gov), plus separate traffic-signs and vision tests; an on-road driving test is required for a first license but not for a learner permit.
exam.languages: NCDMV says the written knowledge test is offered in different languages (specific languages not listed); oral/audio tests are available on request for applicants who have difficulty reading.
exam.retestWait: Applicants who fail the knowledge test or driving test for a regular Class C license may retake it in seven calendar days.
exam.notes: The number of knowledge-test questions is not published on the NCDMV pages checked; 80% correct is required to pass under 19A NCAC 03B .0201 (NC Administrative Code, published by the NC Office of Administrative Hearings, reports.oah.state.nc.us). Teens 15-17 must complete driver education (30 hours classroom + 6 hours behind the wheel) and apply for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit with a parent or guardian present for the written, sign and vision tests; Level 2 requires age 16, 9 months on Level 1, and a 60-hour log (10 at night). Adults 18+ may apply directly for a license or first get a learner permit. Effective Oct. 1, 2026, the Driving Eligibility Certificate requirement was eliminated (SL 2026-46). License renewals and transfers from other states (valid or expired under 2 years) require only the signs and vision tests. The official site does not publish the number of questions; this practice exam uses 40 questions at the official 80% passing standard.

facts.detail: Driving while impaired (DWI) can be proven by showing appreciable impairment from alcohol/drugs, or by a BAC of 0.08 percent or more.

source.quote: By proving the driver's blood alcohol concentration is 0.08 percent or more, or 0.04 or more, if you are driving a Commercial Motor Vehicle.

facts.value: Any amount (zero tolerance)
facts.detail: A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body has the license revoked for one year. Provisional licensees (under 18) face the same any-amount rule.

source.quote: If a driver who is less than 21 years old is convicted for an offense of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body, their license will be revoked for one year.

facts.detail: Commercial motor vehicle drivers are impaired per se at 0.04 BAC; a 0.04+ result brings an immediate 30-day minimum revocation.

source.quote: If your blood alcohol concentration test shows a BAC of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 or more, if you are driving a commercial motor vehicle), your driving privilege will be revoked immediately for a minimum of 30 days.

facts.value: Immediate revocation of at least 30 days plus a minimum 12-month DMV revocation
facts.detail: Refusing a required breath or blood test after a DWI charge means an immediate 30-day (minimum) revocation plus at least 12 months revoked by DMV; a judge may allow limited privileges after six months in some cases.

source.quote: Refusal to perform any required test will result in the immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days and an additional, minimum 12-month revocation by the DMV.

facts.value: Mandatory 1-year license revocation
facts.detail: A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year license revocation; a second within three years brings four years. Restoration after DWI costs $167.25 and the first restoration carries a 0.04 BAC restriction.

source.quote: First conviction: Mandatory revocation of your driver license for a period of one year.

facts.value: Open alcohol containers prohibited, including in the passenger area
facts.detail: NC DWI laws prohibit drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving and transporting an open container, including in the passenger area. In a commercial motor vehicle, even closed containers are banned in the passenger area.

source.quote: Prohibit the transport of an open container of any alcoholic beverage, including in the passenger area of the car;

facts.value: 15 (Level 1 Limited Learner Permit)
facts.detail: Teens 15-17 who have passed an approved driver education course (30 hours classroom + 6 hours behind the wheel) may apply for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit. A regular learner permit is for age 18+.

source.quote: If you are at least 15 years of age and have completed an approved driver education course that meets North Carolina requirements, you may apply for a Level One Limited Learner Permit to operate vehicles requiring a Class C License.

facts.value: 9 months
facts.detail: The Level 1 permit must be held nine months before applying for the Level 2 Limited Provisional License, with no moving-violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the prior six months.

source.quote: You must hold this permit for nine months prior to applying for a Limited Provisional License.

facts.value: 60 hours total, at least 10 at night
facts.detail: The Level 1 driving log must show at least 60 hours, including at least 10 at night, signed by the supervising driver and turned in when applying for the Level 2 license.

source.quote: You will be given a Driving Log to be completed detailing a minimum of 60 hours of operation. At least 10 hours must occur during nighttime hours.

facts.value: Parent, grandparent, guardian, or parent-approved responsible person; licensed at least 5 years
facts.detail: The supervising driver must hold a valid license, have been licensed at least five years, and be seated next to the permit holder (NCDMV Level 1 page). Only the driver and supervising driver may sit in the front seat.

source.quote: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian of the permit/license holder, or a responsible person approved by the parent or guardian. A supervising driver must hold a valid driver license and must have been licensed for at least five years.

facts.value: 16 (Level 2 Limited Provisional License)
facts.detail: Level 2 is for drivers at least 16 but under 18 who held the Level 1 permit nine months. Level 2 must be held six months before Level 3 (Full Provisional).

source.quote: Drivers must be at least 16 years old, but less than 18.

facts.value: Unsupervised driving only 5 a.m.-9 p.m. (Level 2)
facts.detail: Level 2 drivers may drive alone from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., and at any time directly to or from work or volunteer fire/rescue/EMS duty. Level 1 permit holders may drive only 5 a.m.-9 p.m. (with a supervisor) for the first six months.

source.quote: You may drive without supervision from 5 a.m. until 9 p.m. and at any time when driving directly to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service, if you are a member.

facts.value: Unsupervised: only one non-household passenger under 21 (plus one student going to/from school)
facts.detail: When driving unsupervised on a Level 2 license, only one passenger under 21 who is not a household member is allowed; one more under-21 non-household student may ride when going directly to or from school. No limit if all passengers are household members.

source.quote: When driving unsupervised, there may be one passenger that is under 21 that is not a member of the same household as the driver.

facts.value: 18 (regular Class C)
facts.detail: Level 3 Full Provisional License drivers have no time or passenger limits; at 18, eligible drivers may upgrade to a regular Class C license online.

source.quote: At age 18, eligible drivers may upgrade to a regular Class C license online.

facts.value: Texting/email while driving prohibited for all drivers
facts.detail: It is unlawful for any driver to use a cell phone to text or email while operating a vehicle on a public street, highway or public vehicular area. The statutory penalty is a $100 fine plus court costs, with no license points (G.S. 20-137.4A(c)).

source.quote: It is unlawful to use a cell phone for email or text messages while operating a vehicle on a public street or highway or public vehicular area;

facts.value: Drivers under 18: no cell phone use at all while driving
facts.detail: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone or associated technology while driving; exceptions are emergency calls (911/emergency services, parent, legal guardian or spouse per the GDL sections). School bus drivers may not use a cell phone at all while driving the bus.

source.quote: Drivers less than 18 years of age are not permitted to use a cell phone or any additional technology associated with a cell phone while operating a motor vehicle on a public street or highway or public vehicular area while the vehicle is in motion.

facts.value: Driver and all passengers must be belted (front and back)
facts.detail: Everyone in a vehicle made with seat belts must be buckled whenever it moves forward on a street or highway, even if the vehicle has air bags. A child-restraint violation carries 2 license points.

source.quote: The driver and all passengers in a motor vehicle manufactured with seat belts shall have a seat belt properly fastened about their body at all times when the vehicle is in forward motion on a street or highway in this state.

facts.value: Under 8 and under 80 lb: weight-appropriate child restraint; all under 16 restrained
facts.detail: Every passenger under 16 must be in a child restraint or seat belt. A child under 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must be in a weight-appropriate child restraint; with an active front air bag and a rear seat, a child under 5 and under 40 lb must ride in back.

source.quote: A child under age 8 and weighing less than 80 pounds must be properly secured in a weight appropriate child passenger restraint system.

facts.value: Never faster than posted or than is reasonable for conditions
facts.detail: You may not drive faster than the posted limit or faster than is reasonable and wise for existing conditions; often you must drive slower than the posted limit.

source.quote: Never drive faster than the posted speed limit or at a speed that is unreasonable or unwise given the existing conditions.

facts.value: 35 mph in cities and towns unless posted
facts.detail: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit inside cities and towns is 35 mph.

source.quote: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is 35 mph in cities and towns.

facts.value: 55 mph outside cities and towns
facts.detail: The maximum outside cities and towns is 55 mph unless posted otherwise. School buses are limited to 45 mph and school activity buses to 55 mph.

source.quote: Outside cities and towns 55

facts.value: 70 mph
facts.detail: The handbook lists 70 mph as the maximum speed limit for interstates (where posted).

source.quote: For interstates 70

facts.value: Posted minimums: 40 mph in a 55 zone, 45 mph in a 60+ zone (interstate/primary highways)
facts.detail: On interstate and primary highways, where minimum-speed signs are posted, passenger vehicles may not go below 40 mph in a 55 mph zone or 45 mph in a 60 mph or higher zone. Slower drivers must use the far-right lane on multi-lane roads.

source.quote: (1) Forty miles per hour in a speed zone of 55 miles per hour. (2) Forty-five miles per hour in a speed zone of 60 miles per hour or greater. These minimum speeds shall be effective only when appropriate signs are posted indicating the minimum speed.

facts.value: Allowed after a complete stop unless a sign prohibits
facts.detail: After a complete stop at a steady red light you may turn right unless NO TURN ON RED is posted, yielding to traffic and pedestrians. Failing to yield to a pedestrian is a $100-$500 penalty.

source.quote: Unless there is a sign indicating “NO TURN ON RED,” a right turn can be made after coming to a complete stop.

facts.value: Not authorized (only right turns on a steady red)
facts.detail: NC law allows only a right turn after stopping at a steady red light; no left turn on red is authorized, even from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

source.quote: After coming to a complete stop and unless prohibited by an appropriate sign, that approaching vehicle may make a right turn.

facts.value: At least 100 feet; at least 200 feet if speed limit is 45 mph or more
facts.detail: Signal during at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping; if the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal during at least the last 200 feet before turning.

source.quote: Signal at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping. If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet before turning.

facts.value: Pull to the right edge and stop; don't follow/park within one block of fire trucks (400 ft outside city)
facts.detail: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from either direction, drive to the right-hand curb or edge and stop until it passes (except opposite-direction traffic on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median). Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle at a crash, and do not follow or park closer than one block to fire trucks answering an alarm (400 feet outside city limits, G.S. 20-157(c); handbook p. 58).

source.quote: As the emergency vehicle approaches (from ahead or behind), drive to the right-hand curb or edge of the road and stop completely;

facts.value: Change to a non-adjacent lane, or slow down if only one lane
facts.detail: For an emergency or public service vehicle parked or standing within 12 feet of the road with warning lights on: with two or more lanes in your direction, move out of the lane nearest it; with one lane, slow to a reduced safe speed until past. Violation is a $250 infraction (G.S. 20-157(g)).

source.quote: On a highway with only one lane of traffic in the same direction you are traveling, you must slow your speed and drive at a reduced, safe speed until completely past the emergency vehicle.

facts.value: Stop both directions on 2-lane roads, 2-lane with center turn lane, and 4-lane without median; only following traffic stops on 4+ lanes with center turn lane or divided highways with median
facts.detail: Stop when a school bus shows its stop arm or flashing red lights and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn, lights are off and the bus starts moving. Opposing traffic need not stop only on 4+ lane roads with a center turning lane or divided highways of 4+ lanes with a median. Passing a stopped school bus is 5 points.

source.quote: Divided highway of four lanes or more with a median separation: When school bus stops for passengers, only traffic following the bus must stop.

facts.value: Two-second rule
facts.detail: Allow at least two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead passes a point and the time you reach it; increase it in rain (at least twice normal) and around motorcycles.

source.quote: The “two-second rule” says that you should allow two seconds between the time the vehicle ahead of you passes a given point and the time your vehicle reaches the same point.

facts.value: Sunset to sunrise, visibility 400 feet or less, and whenever wipers are on due to weather
facts.detail: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise, when you cannot see 400 feet or more, and whenever windshield wipers are in use because of bad weather.

source.quote: The law requires use of headlights from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less.

facts.value: Dim within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle
facts.detail: When meeting another vehicle, you must dim or tilt your headlight beams so they do not glare into the eyes of people within 500 feet ahead. The handbook says to use low beams in cities and when approaching or following another vehicle.

source.quote: when meeting another vehicle, shall so control the lights of the vehicle operated by him by shifting, depressing, deflecting, tilting, or dimming the headlight beams in such manner as shall not project a glaring or dazzling light to persons within a distance of 500 feet in front of such headlamp.

facts.value: 15 feet
facts.detail: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or the entrance to a fire station.

source.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or entrance to a fire station;

facts.value: Not on a crosswalk
facts.detail: Parking is prohibited on a crosswalk, a sidewalk or a bridge. The handbook does not give a separate distance from crosswalks.

source.quote: On a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge;

facts.value: 25 feet from curb line of intersecting street (15 feet from right-of-way lines if no curb)
facts.detail: Do not park at an intersection, within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street, or within 15 feet of the intersecting right-of-way lines where there is no curb.

source.quote: Within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street or within 15 feet of the intersecting right of way lines if there is no curb;

facts.value: 15 feet from the entrance
facts.detail: Do not park within 15 feet of the entrance to a fire station.

source.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or entrance to a fire station;

facts.value: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
facts.detail: When a signal, lowered gate, flagger or approaching train requires a stop, stop within 50 feet but not closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and do not proceed until safe.

source.quote: the driver of the vehicle shall stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail of the railroad and shall not proceed until he/she can do so safely.

facts.value: Pass only with abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic; safest to change lanes
facts.detail: Bicycles are vehicles. Pass a bicyclist only when there is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic; changing lanes is the safest way, and the vehicle passing laws apply (G.S. 20-149: pass at least 2 feet to the left). In a marked no-passing zone, G.S. 20-150(e) allows passing a bicycle or moped only if you leave at least 4 feet or move completely into the left lane.

source.quote: Drivers wishing to pass a bicyclist may do so only when there is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic is in the opposing lane. The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to change lanes.

facts.value: Yield in marked/unmarked crosswalks at unsignaled intersections; let pedestrians finish crossing
facts.detail: At intersections without signals, pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks have the right of way. Pedestrians crossing on green have the right of way over all vehicles, including turning ones, and if the light changes while a pedestrian is in the street, let them finish crossing.

source.quote: At intersections without traffic signals, pedestrians have the right of way if they are in marked crosswalks or in unmarked crosswalks formed by imaginary lines extending from the sidewalks across the streets;

facts.value: Report immediately to law enforcement if anyone is killed or injured or damage appears to be $1,000 or more
facts.detail: You must immediately report to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency any crash with death, injury, or apparent total property damage of $1,000 or more. Failure to report is 3 points and may lead to suspension.

source.quote: You are required by law to make an immediate report to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency of any crash when any person is killed or injured or the total damage to vehicles and other property appears to amount to $1,000 or more.

facts.detail: Minimum liability coverage is $30,000 for injury to one person, $60,000 for all injuries in a crash, and $25,000 for property damage ($750,000 for a commercial motor vehicle). Coverage must be continuous while the vehicle has a valid plate.

source.quote: $30,000 for injuries to any one person in a crash • $60,000 for all personal injuries in a crash • $25,000 for all property damage in a crash

facts.value: 7 points: may be sent to driver improvement clinic; 12 points in 3 years: suspension
facts.detail: At 7 points you may be assigned a driver improvement clinic ($83.50), which removes 3 points. Reaching 12 points within three years may bring suspension (60 days first, 6 months second, 12 months third); 8 points within three years after reinstatement can bring a second suspension.

source.quote: If you accumulate as many as 12 points within a three-year period, your license may be suspended.

facts.value: Universal: all motorcycle and moped operators and passengers
facts.detail: All motorcycle and moped operators and passengers must wear a helmet that complies with FMVSS 218. A separately applied 'DOT' sticker on a novelty helmet does not make it compliant.

source.quote: All operators and passengers on motorcycles and mopeds must wear a motorcycle safety helmet of a type that complies with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) 218.

notableLaws.title: Provisional licensees: any alcohol or drugs = 1-year revocation
notableLaws.summary: A driver under 18 may not drive after consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs; conviction brings a one-year revocation.

source.quote: It is unlawful for a provisional licensee to drive a motor vehicle after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs — a conviction of such a violation will result in a one-year license revocation.

notableLaws.title: Lose Control/Lose Your License
notableLaws.summary: A student suspended from school (or assigned to an alternative setting for discipline) for more than 10 consecutive days loses the license for 12 months.

source.quote: A loss of license will occur if a student receives a suspension for more than 10 consecutive days or receives an assignment to an alternative educational setting due to disciplinary action for more than 10 consecutive days. This suspension remains in effect for 12 months.

notableLaws.title: Children under 16 may not ride in an open pickup bed
notableLaws.summary: Children under 16 may not ride in the open bed of a pickup unless an exemption applies (adult supervising in the bed, approved seat belt, emergency, parade, agricultural use). Fine $25, no points.

source.quote: North Carolina law prohibits children less than age 16 from riding in the open bed of a pick-up truck.

notableLaws.title: Funeral processions
notableLaws.summary: Same-direction drivers may not pass a funeral procession unless the highway has two or more lanes in that direction; never drive between vehicles in a procession.

source.quote: The driver of a vehicle traveling in the same direction as the funeral procession shall not pass or attempt to pass the funeral procession, except that the operator of such a vehicle may pass a funeral procession when the highway has been marked for two or more lanes of moving traffic in the same direction of the funeral procession.

notableLaws.title: Horn signal when passing; passed driver must help
notableLaws.summary: Passing drivers should blow the horn; the horn places the passed driver under a legal duty to help (move right, never speed up). Speeding up and causing a crash is a misdemeanor. Pass at least 2 feet to the left.

source.quote: The horn signal places the driver of the vehicle you are passing under a legal obligation to help you pass.

notableLaws.title: Dark traffic signal = all-way stop
notableLaws.summary: When a traffic light is out due to a power outage or malfunction, treat the intersection as if there were a stop sign on every approach.

source.quote: When approaching an intersection with a traffic light that has malfunctioned due to a power outage or some other problem, you should approach the intersection and proceed as though the intersection is controlled by a stop sign on all approaches to the intersection.

notableLaws.title: Wipers on, headlights on
notableLaws.summary: Headlights are required whenever windshield wipers are used because of inclement weather.

source.quote: All North Carolina motorists are required to use headlights whenever they are using windshield wipers due to inclement weather.

notableLaws.title: Move vehicles off the travel lane after a non-injury crash
notableLaws.summary: If a crash on a main lane, ramp, shoulder or median has no injuries or deaths, move drivable vehicles out of the travel lane onto the shoulder.

source.quote: If the crash occurred on a main lane, ramp, shoulder, median or adjacent area of the highway and there are no injuries or fatalities, each vehicle should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder of the road provided it can be driven safely under its own power and without causing further damage to the vehicle, other traffic or the roadway.

notableLaws.title: Speeding more than 15 mph over at over 55 mph: 30-day revocation
notableLaws.summary: Conviction of driving more than 15 mph over the limit at a speed above 55 mph revokes the license for at least 30 days; two such convictions in a year, or speeding plus reckless driving on one occasion, bring 60 days.

source.quote: Driving any vehicle more than 15 miles per hour over the speed limit, if you are driving at a speed higher than 55 mph.

notableLaws.title: Provisional licensee suspensions for repeat moving violations
notableLaws.summary: Drivers under 18 face suspension of 30 days for a second moving violation in 12 months, 90 days for a third, and six months for a fourth.

source.quote: 30 days, upon conviction of a second moving violation occurring within a 12-month period;

notableLaws.title: Continuous liability insurance; no grace period
notableLaws.summary: Owners must keep continuous liability insurance while the vehicle has a valid plate; a lapse can lead to plate revocation for 30 days and penalties. Surrender the plate before canceling insurance.

source.quote: North Carolina law requires the owner of every registered vehicle to maintain continuous liability insurance as long as the vehicle has a valid license plate.

notableLaws.title: New residents: 60 days to get an NC license
notableLaws.summary: New residents have 60 days after establishing residence to get an NC license; CDL holders have 30 days. Address and name changes must also be reported within 60 days.

source.quote: A new resident has 60 days after establishing residence to obtain a North Carolina license or learner permit.
